## Installation **Command** ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/card ``` Usage, Action in the header, Content-sized and Section boundaries also render [Button](/components/button). Install it when copying those compositions: ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/button ``` The top preview also renders [Badge](/components/badge): ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/badge ``` **Manual** Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI. 1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed. ```package-manager npm install clsx tailwind-merge ``` 2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers. - [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency. 3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines. | Item | Target file | Full source | | --- | --- | --- | | cadence-utils | `@components/cadence/lib/cn.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) | | card | `@components/cadence/card/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/card.json) | [Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) [Source files: card](https://cadence.dev/r/card.json) 4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition. No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme. Card needs only the two files and packages listed above; no motion runtime, provider or additional item-specific CSS is required. Keep `card/index.tsx` and `lib/cn.ts` at the listed relative paths so the shared `cn` import resolves. Preserve the component's `"use client"` directive: the optional `fit="content"` uses the browser's native `ResizeObserver` to measure content height and apply it immediately, with no interpolation or additional observer package. Before measurement, server-rendered cards use natural content layout. Card has no animation in full, reduced or none mode. For the action compositions, follow [Button's installation](/components/button#installation), including its dependencies and motion setup. To reproduce the top preview, also follow [Badge's installation](/components/badge#installation); the shared `lib/cn.ts` and its packages are already included above. Button and Badge are composition dependencies, not dependencies of Card. Compact renders neither, and the body example snippets do not render Badge, so their unused imports can be omitted. React's `useRef` and `useState` are used only by Content-sized and need no additional package beyond the React setup above; their unused imports in the other snippets can also be omitted. ## Usage ```tsx import { Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardTitle, } from "@/components/cadence/card"; import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button"; export function Plan() { return ( Parity plan 58 components, ten batches, one release train.

Toggle the caller-owned text to compare it with a normal card; the same shell and caller ref remain in place. Narrowing the parent wraps the text and remeasures it. This is geometry, with no animation in any mode. Use it when differing content heights carry information; ordinary card grids usually should line up. ```tsx "use client"; import { useRef, useState } from "react"; import { Badge } from "@/components/cadence/badge"; import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button"; import { Card, CardAction, CardContent, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardTitle } from "@/components/cadence/card"; export function ContentSizedCard() { const [expanded, setExpanded] = useState(false); const fitRef = useRef(null); return (

); } ``` ## Section boundaries Add `border-b` to the header and `border-t` to the footer. The parts already adjust their padding for those boundaries, without introducing another Card part. ```tsx "use client"; import { useRef, useState } from "react"; import { Badge } from "@/components/cadence/badge"; import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button"; import { Card, CardAction, CardContent, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardTitle } from "@/components/cadence/card"; export function CardBoundaries() { return ( Release notesReview the latest changes. Components, fixes and documentation updates. ); } ``` ## When to use - A unit of content that belongs together: a summary, a plan, an account, a record in a grid. - A surface that needs a header, an optional action, body content, and a footer. - A list of comparable items where the boundary itself carries meaning. ## When not to use - To fake spacing. A card is a boundary; use padding if you only need breathing room. - As a page layout. Nesting cards inside cards flattens the hierarchy. - For a modal or a popover; those are overlays with their own focus rules. ## API | Part | Props | Notes | | ----------------- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `Card` | `size`, `fit`, native div props | `size` sets `--card-spacing` and `data-size`; `fit`: `"content"` hugs the content. | | `CardHeader` | native div props | Grid header; reacts to `CardAction` and a bottom border. | | `CardTitle` | native div props | Bold, leading-none. Does not create a heading. | | `CardDescription` | native div props | Muted supporting text. | | `CardAction` | native div props | Top-right slot inside the header. | | `CardContent` | native div props | Body; carries the horizontal padding. | | `CardFooter` | native div props | Bottom row; reacts to a top border. | Every part sets `data-slot`, so CSS can reach it: `[&>[data-slot=card-header]]:gap-4`. Under `fit="content"` the parts are wrapped in one `data-slot="card-flow"` box, which is the element the height is measured from — style the parts from the shell as before, and the flow box only if you need the measured layer itself. ## Motion contract No motion (T0). A card does not fade, lift, or scale in. If a group of cards should appear in sequence, that is a page-level `list.stagger` decision made by the parent, not a property of the card. `fit="content"` adds no row to the table below: the measured height is applied as soon as it is known, so there is no phase, no interpolation, and no reduced-motion branch to keep — the geometry is information, and both modes render it identically. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- | | – | none | – | – | | reduced | none | – | – | | none | none | – | – | ## Accessibility - `Card` is a plain `div`: no role, no landmark. That is correct for a visual grouping — but it means the card is not a navigable region. If a set of cards is the main content, wrap it in a `
` or a list (`
    /
  • `). - `CardTitle` renders a `div`. When the title belongs in the document outline, put a heading inside it: `

    Parity plan

    `, or render the card with `aria-labelledby` pointing at the title's id. - A card that is clickable must contain a real link or button; do not put `onClick` on the card and call it done — it is invisible to keyboard users. ## Responsiveness and performance Cards follow their parent layout by default. The caller owns grid columns and narrow-screen wrapping; size="sm" changes spacing, not a breakpoint. With fit="content", CSS resolves width and a ResizeObserver measures content height after mount, applying it immediately without interpolation. SSR uses natural content layout before measurement. T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. This wrapper renders HTML/CSS; interactive children and application handlers still need their own client code. The optional Card observer is client code and is disconnected on cleanup. Server-rendered markup does not imply that every interaction works without JavaScript. The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for this item's own shipped source; dependencies and application bundles are measured separately. ## Notes for AI - Use `CardFooter` for actions, not a bare `div` — it keeps spacing consistent when `size` changes. - Do not add hover lift to a card that is not interactive. Motion on a static card is decoration (P9). - `fit="content"` is opt-in and per card. A grid of cards is meant to line up; only reach for the content-sized variant when the differences between cards are the information.
